messages.content: Should I stop paying rent until they fix the heat?

message.content: I need to give you the legal context first, and then connect you with someone who can advise on your specific situation.

Here is what the published law says:

**NY Real Property Law § 235-b** (https://www.nysenate.gov/legislation/laws/RPP/235-B) requires that every residential lease carries an **implied warranty that the premises are fit for human habitation** and free of conditions dangerous to life, health or safety. You cannot waive this by lease — any agreement waiving it is void as contrary to public policy.

**NYC heat and hot water standards** (https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-01036):
- During heat season (Oct 1–May 31): Between 6 AM and 10 PM, inside temperature must be at least 68°F when outside is below 55°F. Between 10 PM and 6 AM, it must be at least 62°F at all times.
- Hot water must be supplied year-round at a minimum of 120°F.

These are violations of the warranty of habitability if the landlord knew or should have known and did not repair them within a reasonable time.

**What you should document as evidence:**
- Dates and times the heat or hot water was out
- Indoor temperature readings from a thermometer, photographed with a timestamp
- Every 311 complaint number and the date filed
- Written notice to the landlord and the date sent (the warranty generally requires the landlord to have notice and a reasonable opportunity to repair)

**The official complaint route:**
- File with 311 (https://portal.311.nyc.gov/), which creates a dated public record and can trigger an HPD inspection
- If conditions persist, an HP Action in Housing Court is the route tenants use to ask a judge to order repairs

---

**I am giving you published law and this building's public record, not legal advice about your situation.** Whether you should withhold rent, how long is "reasonable," and what you can do depends on the facts of your case—your lease, when you noticed it, whether you notified the landlord in writing, how long it has been, and whether you are in a protected tenancy. **These organisations can advise you and confirm whether the law applies to you:**

- **Met Council on Housing — Tenants Rights Hotline**: 212-979-0611 (Mon/Wed 1:30–8pm, Fri 1:30–5pm) — one of the few places to call with a single question
- **The Legal Aid Society — Housing**: Central 212-577-3300 (or borough numbers at https://legalaidnyc.org/get-help/housing-problems/) — free legal advice and representation
- **NYC 311**: 311 or 212-639-9675 (24/7) — file a heat complaint immediately

Call one of these today with your situation. They will tell you what you can do.
